Sylvia Garcia

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 29, Harris County, Texas · Incumbent

U.S. Representative for Texas' 29th Congressional District; attorney

Sylvia Garcia is the Democratic incumbent for Texas' 29th Congressional District and has held the seat since 2019. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary against Jarvis Johnson and Robert Slater. She faces Republican Martha Fierro in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Garcia stands

Economy and inflation
Says rising health premiums, rent and grocery prices have made daily life unaffordable. Supports organized labor and opposes cuts to Medicaid, Medicare and programs that help families with expenses.
Housing
Supports helping first-time homebuyers and increasing the number of affordable housing units, working through the House Financial Services Housing Subcommittee.
Health care
Opposes Medicaid and Medicare cuts. Says rising health care premiums are making life unaffordable for families.
Immigration and border security
Lead sponsor of the Dream and Promise Act, which would create a path to citizenship for Dreamers. Supports expanding Temporary Protected Status and opposes Texas' Operation Lone Star spending.
Immigration enforcement oversight
Called for an independent investigation of a July 2026 ICE shooting in Houston, led a Democratic forum on it, and urged a 10-point set of immigration enforcement reforms.
Worker safety
Plans to introduce a federal bill on heat and injury risks for construction workers, named for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Houston man killed by an immigration agent.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas' 29th District, 2019–present
  • Texas State Senate, 2013–2018
  • Harris County Commissioners Court (former commissioner)
  • Houston City Controller (former)
  • Director and presiding judge, Houston Municipal Court system (former)
  • Former social worker and legal aid lawyer
  • J.D., Thurgood Marshall School of Law, Texas Southern University, 1978
  • B.A. in social work and political science, Texas Woman's University, 1972
  • Born 1950, San Diego, Texas
